newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks slide on property, banks selldown.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks slide on property, banks selldown.

text.p: Manila stocks tumbled at the close on Monday due to foreign selldown on property and bank issues, traders said.

"It was really a bloodbath. There were 133 losers and 17 gainers," said Raymond Garcia, president at Diversified Securities. The main index crashed below its 3,000-level support to end at 2,990.96 points, down 69.63 points or 2.28 percent.
The main index hit a day's low of 2,979.62 points.
"(Some) foreign brokerage firms put the Philippine market on their negative list," said Garcia.
Traders said foreign investors were concerned over the state of the Philippine property and banking sectors, and the lack of a clear successor to President Fidel Ramos in 1998.

"I think what the market sees is a shift in our sentiment from one that is more optimistic to one that is seriously cautious," said Joey Salceda, director at SBC Warburg, a unit of Swiss Banking Corp.
"The (Philippine stock market) is far from a bust but we have given up on a bull run this year," Salceda added.
Other traders said negative reports of rising auto loans and credit cards in local banks and the Victorias Milling Corp loan crisis fuelled fears on the lending prudence of local banks.
Rumours of financial difficulties in Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc and its Unit Empire East land Holdings Inc, despite repeated denials by the companies, sent property stocks down.
All indices dropped, with the property and banking sectors, posting the heaviest losses.
